plain_description.what: Token counts were estimated per model and per cell with tokenizer proxies. A router that picks the cheapest model within 0.5 points of the best model in each cell was then scored out of sample. It needed to reach 85% or less of the best model's token cost. No LLM calls were made.
plain_description.why: It tests whether per-cell routing can save money as well as keep accuracy.
plain_description.information: Passing would show a real cost saving from routing. Failing would mean the savings exist only on a rough parameter-count proxy. Result: done, FAIL, and robust to the choice of tokenizer. Accuracy was kept (+0.54 points, interval covering 0). Cost was 98.8% of the best model's, a saving of only about 1%, because the top tier often has only one model. The re-read on all 52 cells is undetermined. Latency was not computed.
